signature.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
signature.detail: The embalmed body of Vietnam's founding father lies in a vast granite mausoleum on Ba Dinh Square, a pilgrimage site for locals and a sober must-see for visitors. Go early morning (closed Mondays and Fridays, and for several weeks each autumn); dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered, and leave cameras and bags at the entrance.

signature.name: Hanoi Old Quarter
signature.detail: A dense maze of 36 historic guild streets where motorbikes, street vendors and colonial shophouses collide—the best place to feel Hanoi's energy. Wander on foot in the late afternoon or early evening when the heat eases and the beer corners fill up.

signature.name: Temple of Literature
signature.detail: Vietnam's first university, founded in 1070, with tranquil courtyards, stone stelae and Confucian temples—one of the city's most beautiful and historic sites. Visit early to beat the tour groups; tickets are cheap and the grounds are shady.

signature.name: Imperial Citadel of Thang Long
signature.detail: A UNESCO-listed complex of royal palaces, gates and bunkers that layers a thousand years of Vietnamese history. The site is large and exposed, so go in the cooler morning hours and allow at least two hours.

signature.name: One Pillar Pagoda
signature.detail: A tiny wooden pagoda perched on a single stone pillar, rebuilt after French destruction and now an icon of Hanoi. It sits near the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, so combine the two in one early-morning outing.

signature.name: St. Joseph's Cathedral
signature.detail: A neo-Gothic cathedral that looks straight out of Europe, surrounded by cafés and a lively square in the Old Quarter. Open outside mass times; dress respectfully and climb the bell tower if you can.

signature.name: Hoan Kiem Lake
signature.detail: The heart of Hanoi, where locals jog at dawn and the red Huc Bridge leads to Ngoc Son Temple on a tiny island. Come at sunrise for tai chi and calm, or at night when the lake is lit up.
